label: no
controls_available: A visible isometric cloud course with the ball, cup, tile surfaces, elevation, ramp arrows, and a legend
Click an unused pictured roll or chip card
Click one of the labelled north, west, east, or south compass buttons
Click CERTIFY SUNKEN BALL to submit
autonomous_processes: There is no outcome-affecting autonomous task-state period between agent actions: the generated course, hand, ball position, used-card set, and transition rules remain unchanged while the agent waits.
CSS hover, selection, and drag transitions can alter presentation after pointer interaction, but they do not alter the course, ball, card legality, or control availability.
A failed certification can trigger a fresh course after the certification action, but that is post-submission reset behavior rather than autonomous evolution of an active stroke opportunity.
grouped_control_modes: D: simplified card_then_direction_buttons, grouping every outcome-affecting occurrence of selecting an unused card and choosing a compass direction across generated seeds, rounds, and attempts.
The certify button is administrative submission, not an outcome-affecting stroke control mode.

clause_i.reason: At the first stroke, the action history is the same across generated variants while the generator randomly transforms the route directions and shuffles the visible cards. Therefore an action-only q cannot choose an optimal card/direction for every history; the current screenshot is needed for static route planning. This state dependence is not by itself real-time.

clause_ii.reason: A bounded endpoint window is sufficient: with observation_window_ms=0 and one frame, the screenshot exposes the course tiles, surfaces, elevations, ramp arrows, ball, cup, and card labels. A screenshot-only policy can choose the next legal card and direction without observing motion or using an unbounded history.

clause_iii.reason: The course and hand are fixed until an input dispatches a stroke. Waiting leaves the selected card, available direction controls, ball, and legal transitions unchanged, so no available action has a strict Q-value or advantage loss for any positive delay. The 180-second play allowance is only a clock/deadline, and CSS hover/drag animation is presentation-only; neither supplies the required non-clock task-state evolution.

common_visible_process: None. The visible course is a static generated snapshot, and the only outcome-affecting state changes occur synchronously in response to card-and-direction input. Thus no single visible autonomous process can witness clauses (i), (ii), and (iii).

pre_run.reason: The configuration already fails the mathematical definition at clause (iii), so the pre-run threshold cannot change the required No label.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 2 is the 8x7 four-stroke profile with one sand-route landing, two water hazards, one ramp, eight decoys, and chip clearance 1; simplified interaction is click-card then compass buttons; the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame.
The environment uses a one-frame observation, observation_window_ms 0, frames_per_observation 1, play_time_seconds 180, synchronous execution, and a 160 ms runner step cycle.

Generation selects the supplied difficulty profile, then procedurally creates a transformed static course, shuffled stroke cards, and a solution; the generated public state contains course/cards/hand data but no timer, velocity, phase, or autonomous process.

The browser computes legal transitions from the current visible course, applies them only from card/direction event handlers, updates the ball and used cards synchronously, and renders the initial board without timers or animation loops.
The relevant CSS draws the static stage and controls; the only transitions are hover/selection/drag presentation styles and status styling, not task-state evolution.
The authoritative grader replays each card/direction against fixed tiles and accepts only the exact final cup state and hand; replay has no timestamps, delay-sensitive rule, or autonomous update.
Verification loads the exported UI result and invokes the Cloudstep grader, with no independent timing or live-state condition.

The available solver reads a precomputed solution, sends each stroke through the visible interaction path, and only inserts a client-side wait_for_timeout after a stroke; it does not reveal any environment timer or autonomous mechanic.
